name: California Watershed Protection Fund

funder.name: Rose Foundation for Communities and the Environment

summary: Grants funded by Clean Water Act settlements for water-quality stewardship, watershed restoration and protection projects in eligible California watersheds, which change from cycle to cycle.

eligibility.rule: Be a 501(c)(3), fiscally sponsored by one, governmental or tribal entity
Demonstrate a strong track record of community-based water quality stewardship
Show known interconnectivity to surface waters for exclusively groundwater projects
Have no active grant from this fund when reapplying
Past grantees may reapply in the next cycle after their grant report is submitted and approved
Project benefits surface water quality of an eligible watershed
No endowment, land acquisition or general operations. Capital improvements must directly improve water quality.
Can complete the project and has successfully delivered similar or related work

applicant_types.quote: The applicant must be a 501(c)3 organization, fiscally-sponsored by a 501(c)3, or a governmental or tribal entity. Non-profit colleges, universities, university clinics and graduate programs are eligible to apply

geography.quote: The California Watershed Protection Fund supports projects designed to improve water quality and protect watersheds across California.

access.quote: Applications must be submitted by 5 PM on the due date.

window.quote: Eligible geographies for this fund vary cycle to cycle due to funding fluctuations.

amount.quote: The maximum grant amount is $40,000 with most grants expected to range between $10,000 and $30,000.

fiscal_sponsor.quote: The applicant must be a 501(c)3 organization, fiscally-sponsored by a 501(c)3, or a governmental or tribal entity.

effort.quote: Interested applicants must create an account and submit an application via our online application system.

eligibility.quote: The applicant must be a 501(c)3 organization, fiscally-sponsored by a 501(c)3, or a governmental or tribal entity.
All applicants must be able to demonstrate a strong track record of community-based, water quality stewardship.
Projects focusing exclusively on groundwater quality are only eligible if there is known interconnectivity to surface waters.
Organizations with an active grant from this fund are not eligible to reapply.
Organizations that have been funded may only re-apply in the next cycle after their grant report has been submitted and approved.
Projects must benefit the surface water quality of the watershed in question.

Endowment, land acquisition, capital improvement (unless proposed project directly improves water quality) or other similar projects. Grants to individuals or for-profit businesses. Grants for general operating support.
The applicant must demonstrate the capacity to complete the proposed project, including experience in successfully conducting similar or otherwise related work in the past.

after_award.quote: If your group is awarded a grant, you must provide a final grant report at the completion of your project. If your project is longer than one year, you must provide an interim report as well.
